summary: The Cambridge Trust International Scholarship supports highly ranked postgraduate applicants to the University of Cambridge who come from any country except the UK and Ireland. There is no separate scholarship application: you apply for admission and ask to be considered for funding. The award pays the international-rate tuition fee, annual maintenance for a single person, the student visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge, plus further unnamed benefits. The 2027/28 funding listing shows it as a PhD award with about 60 places.
eligibility_notes:
Open to applicants from all countries except the UK and Ireland, with overseas (international) fee status. The applicant must be highly ranked by the prospective Cambridge department. Any subject is accepted, except premium rate courses (the Trust names the MBA and MFin as examples of courses it does not fund).

Selection rests on academic ability, research potential, examination results and references. The scholarship page says the applicant's financial situation does not affect selection, but the Trust describes its funding as for students with financial need and the funding listing names both financial need (including hardship) and academic merit as the basis. Read both statements together and expect the offer letter to settle it.

General Trust rules for postgraduate awards: you need a conditional offer of admission; no funding is given for a degree at the same level as, or lower than, one you already hold (an exception is a second MPhil that is required before PhD consideration); students part-way through a Cambridge course cannot apply unless they are applying for a higher degree after graduating. Cambridge's own minimum for entry is a 2:1 UK Bachelor's degree or an international equivalent, and many courses ask for more. The Trust says applicants are not treated less favourably on grounds such as sex, marital status, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or age.

Language: if English is not your first language, your course may need a test; see the requirements list. Part-time study can be considered where the University offers it, and the listing shows full-time and part-time study.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work-experience requirement is stated. The Trust says applicants are not treated less favourably because of age.
funding_summary: The scholarship covers the University tuition fee at the international rate, annual maintenance described as sufficient for a single person, the student visa and the Student Immigration Health Surcharge, plus "various additional benefits" that the page does not itemise. For a PhD, the Trust will, on application, give up to a further 6 months of maintenance to help with writing up. The length of the award is not stated on the pages read; extension for PhD scholars is up to 6 months, and no funding beyond 3.5 years is given.
programmes_note: Any subject at Cambridge except premium rate courses. The 2027/28 funding listing says the award applies to 114 courses; the list sits behind a link that did not open in the page text, so the courses cannot be copied here.
institutions_note: University of Cambridge only. The award can be held at any Cambridge College. On the application you may name up to two Colleges or leave it blank; the Trust does not choose the College or arrange accommodation. Some other funds are tied to a College, but this one is not.

summary.detail: The 2027/28 funding listing states the level of study as PhD, full-time or part-time, with about 60 awards, 114 courses covered, and up to a further 6 months of maintenance for writing up on application.

Not confirmed for this award. The Trust's general postgraduate page says it funds Masters-level and PhD study, and the scholarship page itself names no level, but the 2027/28 funding listing for this award names PhD only. Treat Master's as unconfirmed.
summary.source_text: scholarship page names no degree level

benefits.limit_text: University tuition fee at the international rate
benefits.conditions: Any Cambridge College. College fee is not listed for this award.

benefits.limit_text: Annual maintenance sufficient for a single person (no amount is given on the pages read)
benefits.conditions: PhD scholars may apply for up to 6 more months of maintenance to write up; the Trust gives no funding beyond 3.5 years. The Trust generally gives no extra allowance for spouses, children or dependants.

The scholarship page lists the visa. The Trust's guidance for awardees says most scholars pay for their own visa and Immigration Health Surcharge and that the offer letter states whether the Trust covers them, so check the offer letter.
Listed on the scholarship page; see the visa note above.
Not described on the scholarship page or the funding listing.

benefits.limit_text: Travel is paid only if the offer letter says so
benefits.conditions: Scholars otherwise arrange and pay for their own travel and accommodation.

benefits.limit_text: Additional funding for current scholars on request
benefits.conditions: Extension of maintenance (PhD, up to 6 months, apply no later than one month before the award ends); hardship funding for unforeseen events; conference funding of up to GBP 500 for PhD scholars on a full scholarship, with supervisor approval. Not paid: childcare and dependant costs, direct research costs, private medical expenses. The Trust does not pay for pre-sessional language courses.

requirements.text: Cambridge postgraduate admissions application submitted through the Applicant Portal by your course's funding deadline, with the funding section completed to say you wish to be considered for funding. A conditional offer of admission is needed. Each course needs its own application and documents. Agents' applications are not accepted. The application must be in English and Latin script.
Declare significant income from all sources (salaries, business profit, rents, dividends) in the funding section; the Trust says many awards need evidence of financial need.

Academic transcripts and certificates for every degree you have taken. If you are still studying, an interim or unofficial transcript is accepted and the final one is needed after an offer. Upload scanned originals; originals may be checked later through a verification service.

Two referees, entered in the Applicant Portal. They upload references in English through the Referee Portal by the application deadline; email and post are not accepted. Referees should be academic or professional depending on how long ago you left higher education (two academic referees if you are studying or left within 3 years). Do not name PhD students.
Curriculum vitae or resume, uploaded with the application.
Personal statement describing your skills, experience, academic achievements and motivation for the course.
Research proposal giving the topic, how it extends existing work, why it matters and why it is feasible in the time and resources available. A separate proposal is needed for each course.
requirements.conditional_rule: Most research courses (including PhD) require one

requirements.text: English test result (IELTS Academic, IELTS for UKVI Academic, IELTS One Skill Retake, IELTS Online, TOEFL iBT including Home Edition, or C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency for some courses). Scores come from the course page. Results must be dated no more than 2 years before the course starts. Test reports sent directly by IELTS or TOEFL are not accepted, and scores from different certificates cannot be combined.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if English is not your first language and not exempt (exemptions apply to nationals educated in a majority English-speaking country, or graduates of a 3-year UK-equivalent degree from such a country, excluding Canada). For most courses evidence is needed only after an offer.

requirements.text: Non-English documents must come with a full translation by a registered translator; do not translate them yourself. Upload PDFs under 2MB, not encrypted. Hard copies are not accepted.
Written work samples for courses that ask for them. GRE only if the course page says it is required; GMAT is not accepted by any course.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if the course page asks

requirements.text: Latest passport and any current or previous UK visas, uploaded to the Self-Service account after an offer so that the University can prepare the Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies.
requirements.conditional_rule: After an offer, for applicants who need a student visa

requirements.text: Application fee: GBP 20 per applicant for doctoral courses (up to 7 applications per entry year) and GBP 85 per application for other postgraduate courses, paid by Visa or MasterCard before submitting; a fee waiver may apply. The Trust cannot help with fees or waivers.

application_steps.title: Choose your course and find its funding deadline
application_steps.detail: Pick a course in the Cambridge postgraduate directory and note its funding deadline, which is different from the application deadline. The main University funding deadlines for 2027/28 entry are 8 December 2026 and 6 January 2027; your course may differ. The complete application, including references, must be in by 23:59 GMT on the deadline.

application_steps.title: Check the Trust's rules and name up to two Colleges
application_steps.detail: Read the Trust's eligibility rules and the scholarship listing. You may name up to two Colleges or leave it blank; the Trust does not select the College. Apply for every scholarship that suits you, because funding is highly competitive. Some partner awards need a separate partner application; this scholarship does not.

application_steps.title: Submit the admissions application and ask for funding
application_steps.detail: In the Applicant Portal fill every section, upload your documents, pay the fee and tick that you wish to apply for funding. Declare significant income. No separate scholarship form is needed; the Trust cannot add information after you submit, though extra documents can be uploaded to your self-service account.

application_steps.title: Department assesses your admission application
application_steps.detail: The department or faculty reviews your application, may interview you and recommends admission. The Degree Committee approves (about 10 days) and the Postgraduate Admissions Office issues a conditional offer (about 10 days, longer at peak times). Admission offers start from November at the earliest.

application_steps.title: Trust selects scholars from ranked applicants
application_steps.detail: The award goes to applicants highly ranked by their department, judged on academic ability, research potential, examination results and references. The Trust does not take part in admission, College choice or departmental ranking. The awarding period runs from mid-February to the end of July; most awards are made in February and March, and partner awards that involve interviews are often decided April to June.

application_steps.title: Wait for the offer; no news by end of July means unsuccessful
application_steps.detail: The Trust gives no updates on individual applications and will say on its website when main offers are finished. Awards not taken up are reallocated, so you stay under consideration until the end of July. If you have not heard by then, assume you were unsuccessful. Unsuccessful applicants are not notified and get no individual feedback.

application_steps.title: Return the response form and meet admission conditions
application_steps.detail: Read the offer letter and keep a copy; it may serve as proof of funding for a student visa. Return the response form before its deadline, because the scholarship is not final until the Trust has it. Meet all admission conditions on time (for an October start, the conditions deadline is 31 July) and accept the admission offer in the Self-Service account.

application_steps.title: Arrange visa, travel and arrival
application_steps.detail: Obtain a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies from the University (expected in June for an October start) and apply for the student visa, with ATAS clearance if your course needs it. Plan your own accommodation and travel unless your offer letter says otherwise, and do not make non-refundable bookings before admission is confirmed.

application_steps.title: Keep the Trust informed during the award
application_steps.detail: Scholarships must be taken up in the year awarded and usually cannot be deferred. Tell the Trust about any other funding offered before or during the award, since a full-cost award from another source (except Gates Cambridge or Harding, which also end the Trust offer) can end the Trust offer. Extension, hardship and conference funding can be requested on forms.
